title: EGY-12 · News: comment on the news and follow a talk show

blocks.text: EGY-12 · News: comment on the news and follow a talk
show
Lesson overview

Egyptians talk about current affairs everywhere: at coffee, in taxi, in the family, on social media. And in the TV talk shows, which are among the most followed programs in the Arab world, the conductor opens in fuṣḥā, the guest responds in Egyptian, and the conversation passes from one to the other also in the same sentence. In this unity you learn to speak of a news in Egyptian (what happened, what you think, what people say), to recognize the Egyptian caught up in debates, with the words of the fuṣḥā pronounced to the Egyptian (saqāfa, istismār, qānūn), to take and defend the word in a discussion and to distinguish a news from a voice (išāʿa) when it circulates on social media. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-03, B2-04 and B2-05.

rows: 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 166–174), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, extracts of talk shows or current Egyptian programs (Appendix C)
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. report and comment on news in Egyptian, distinguishing facts, opinions and voices;
2. recognizing the words of fuṣḥā in the Egyptian pronunciation read ( ⁧ث⁩ → s, ⁧ذ⁩ → z, ⁧ق⁩ → q in translated words);
3. follow a short extract of talk show where fuṣḥā and Egyptians alternate;
4. take the floor, politely interrupt and defend its position in a debate;
5. ask and verify the source of news circulating on social media.
Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

3. The educated Egyptian
When they talk about serious topics, Egyptians use many words of the fuṣḥāBut they pronounce them according to regular rules.

ʾalb Heart of heart of heart of heart il-iqtiṣād, il-qānūn, il-qaḍiyya

blocks.text: ⁧ج⁩ g g (also in translated words) gamīl · il-maglis, il-gumhuriyya

Two pronunciations of the same word. Some words have a daily form and a translated: ʾaḍiyya / qaḍiyya The following points are added: ʾānūn / qānūn "Law" is replaced by the following: il-ʾAhira / al-Qāhira Cairo. The form with q is felt in the news, in the official speeches, in the questions of the conductor; the shape with ʾ in the house and on the street. Recognizing both of them is essential for listening. The mixed register. In a debate a sentence can begin in Egyptian and end up in fuṣḥā: ana šāyif inn il-mušikla, fī al-ḥaqīqa, muškilat taḫṭīṭ In my opinion, the problem is actually a planning problem. The parties to the fuṣḥā are often formulas ( ⁧في الحقيقة⁩ , ⁧من ناحية أخرى⁩ , ⁧بشكل عام⁩ ) or technical terms.

8. Listen to the authentic news

What to choose. Short extracts (3–5 minutes) of current Egyptian programs: talk shows, street interviews on daily themes (prices, transport, school), services in which people comment a news. At first, it avoids very heated debates, where we all speak together. See Appendix C. The method for a talk show extract.
1. The painting. Who is this (conductor, guest, phone call)? About what? Write the theme in a sentence.
2. The two records. Listen and mark where you speak in fuṣḥā and where in Egyptian: who changes, when, why?
3. Positions. For each person, write his position in a sentence and keyword he uses.
4. The review. Report the extract in Egyptian in one minute (il-barnāmig itkallim ʿan…, iḍ-ḍēf ʾāl inn...), then in Italian in three sentences, with attributions.
9. Pronunciation

The words translated. Read with the tutor alternating the two pronunciations: ʾaḍiyya / qaḍiyya · ʾānūn / qānūn · talāta / ṯalāṯa (fuṣḥā) / is-saqāfa (English read). In Egyptian read the ⁧ث⁩ is never pronounced as in fuṣḥā (ṯ): becomes s. The tone of the conductor. The conductor shall give the fuṣḥā the opening at a slow and steady pace; When it passes to the Egyptian, it accelerates and changes melody. Imitates the passage: masāʾ al-ḫayr… natanāwal al-layla... / ṭab, ya duktūr, ḥaḍritak šāyif ēh?
